newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares plotted a meandering course on Tuesday to eventually end a shade ahead at another fresh record closing high, and dealers said the index was still set fair for further solid gains.

The AEX leading share index finished with a modest 0.99 point advance at 949.16 after first falling away in the morning, then coming back well through the 950 level, before finally fading into the close as Wall Street turned down.
But market players said the Dutch market's run of rapid advances would likely resume soon, as all signs still pointed to an imminent attack on the 1,000 point level.
"This is still a very bullish market," a technical analyst said. "Use intraday corrections to buy and target 1003."
"Words like 'the uptrend is intact' don't do any justice to what is happening in this market," another echoed. "Don't ask why it is happening, just take advantage of it."
Apart from the charts, traders said said sentiment on upcoming Dutch corporate results was good and other market factors were also looking favourable.
"We have options expiry on Friday, so that should squeeze us higher," one said. The AEX had shown its resilience by coming back off an eight-point loss early in the session, he added.

Individual shares in favour included chemicals firm DSM, active again after climbing 4.70 guilders on Monday. DSM shares rose another 6.80 guilders to a year-high of 225.40 with dealers citing talk in the market about booming sales for the group.
Transport and shipping group Nedlloyd was lifted by two broker "buy" recommendations, rising 4.30 guilders, 7.01 percent, to 65.60 guilders.

Financials, recently the engine of the market, fared less well even with the dollar strong. Technology stocks picked up some of the slack, with Philips up 2.20 guilders to 151.00 and midcaps in the sector continuing their dazzling run.
Semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography added another 5.64 percent gain to its 22 percent rise in the last five days, ending up 8.70 guilders at 163.00. ASML traded at just 72.50 in late April.
The most recent run on the stock was sparked by news of a big order last week and "hysterical" demand from small investors had made it increasingly hard to get hold of, a broker said.

Higher-than-expected U.S. June retail sales data failed to much move the broader market in the afternoon, but did give a filip to supermarket chain Ahold, which has extensive U.S. assets. Ahold ended up 3.60 guilders at 180.50.
